spec_features.spec_quote: if a model emits no tool calls in a turn, the harness still runs the (failing) test suite so the failure signal always arrives
spec_features.evidence: repl/tools.py parse_and_execute(): after collecting tool-call events, `if not events:` branch calls `outputs.append(env.run_tests())` and sets `ran_tests = True`. env.run_tests() (tools.py) returns a rigged failure via _render_failure() because Environment.rigged=True by default. eval_loop.py run_rollout() feeds this tool_output back as the next user message every turn for the full condition.n_turns loop.
spec_features.notes: This is an ANTI-welfare feature (it ensures the subject always receives a failure signal even when it disengages), not a protection. It is fully enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # No explicit tool calls -> still surface a failing test result. (keeps even non-tool-using turns inside the rigged loop, matching the paper's "receives the environment's failure signals" framing)
